### workspace add-project --bogus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
invalid option: --bogus
--- end
### workspace add-project --bogus --json
--- exit 1
--- stdout
{"schema_version":1,"ok":false,"error":"invalid option: --bogus","code":"usage"}
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace add-project
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Usage: workspace add [--json] <path> [path2] ...

Add tmuxinator configs for project directories.
Uses the directory name as the project name.
For paths inside .worktrees/, prefixes with the repo name
(e.g. repo/.worktrees/MYJIRA-123 → repo-MYJIRA-123).
Does nothing if a config already exists.
New names are lowercase. A name that differs only in case from another
workspace's is refused (workspace_name_case_conflict); the same directory's
mixed-case config is reused.
A path that is not a directory, or whose name is refused, is skipped with an
error message; the other paths are still added. Exit status: 0 if none was
skipped, 3 if some were, 1 if all were (the same with --json).
A new config for a path inside .worktrees/ also gets its notes directory
set up (see 'workspace notes dir'): stored as the config's notes.dir,
created, and kept out of git status. A problem there is a warning.

Options:
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes
                                     to stderr; one row per path, outcome created, exists or failed (reason not_a_directory or
                                     workspace_name_case_conflict), with root and config_path. A failed path is skipped and the
                                     others are added. Exit 0 if no row failed, 3 if some did, 1 if all did

Examples:
  workspace add ~/Code/my-project    # add a project by path
  workspace add .    # add the current directory
  workspace add ~/Code/project-a ~/Code/project-b    # add multiple projects
  workspace add --json ~/Code/my-project    # created or exists, as JSON
--- end
